hints.title: Distance Metric Count Monotonicity
hints.text: Sorting the array organizes differences naturally. As distance threshold d increases, the total count of pairs with difference at most d increases monotonically.

hints.title: Sliding Boundary Pair Counting Invariant
hints.text: On a sorted array, for each right index, advancing a left pointer while the difference exceeds d allows counting all valid pairs ending at right in amortized linear time.

hints.title: Distance Threshold Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Sort the array. Set the minimum distance to zero and the maximum distance to the difference between first and last elements. Repeatedly pick the midpoint distance and count pairs using a sliding window. If the count is at least k, reduce the upper limit; otherwise raise the lower limit.

complexity.time: O(N log N + N log D)
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N + N log D) time and O(log N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all N * (N - 1) / 2 pair distances takes O(N^2) time and causes memory limits when using a heap for large N.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting takes O(N log N) time, followed by bisection over distance in O(N log(max_dist)) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize how sorting transforms the pair count verification into a two-pointer linear pass.
